#### List:

- Intro
- Filtration
- Reabsorption
- Secretion

#### Intro:

+--------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Normal values            | - ECF 3.5-5mM (tight control required for cell function)        |
|                          | - ICF 150mM                                                     |
|                          | - Intake 1-1.5mmol/kg/day                                       |
|                          | - Output: urine \>\> faeces, sweat                              |
+--------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Renal potassium handling | - Freely filtered                                               |
|                          | - Fixed fraction reabsorbed (\~95%)                             |
|                          | - Variable secretion                                            |
|                          | - Small amount compulsory excretion (5%)                        |
+--------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Significance             | - Lower priority than sodium reabsorption                       |
|                          | - Compulsory excretion means compulsory intake \~0.5mmol/kg/day |
+--------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Filtration:

+-------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Freely filtered   | - 180L/day x 4mM = 720mmol/day                                                                    |
+-------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Minimal variation | - Minimal variation in ECF concentration                                                          |
|                   | - Minimal variation in GFR: autoregulation to 125mL/min                                           |
|                   |   - Myogenic: ↓afferent arteriolar stretch → reflex dilatation (effective for mAP 70-170mmHg)     |
|                   |   - Chemical (tubuloglomular feedback): ↓NaCl at distal tubule → reflex dilatation                |
|                   |   - Hormonal (renin-angiotensin): ↓afferent arteriolar stretch or ↓NaCl at distal tubule → ↑renin |
+-------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Reabsorption:

+------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Proximal tubule  | - Paracellular transit:                                                                                                                                   |
|                  |   - Solvent drag                                                                                                                                          |
| (65%)            |   - Passive diffusion                                                                                                                                     |
|                  |                                                                                                                                                           |
|                  | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/12/prize-image001.jpg){fig-alt="Proximal tubular potassium reabsorption through solvent drag and paracellular diffusion"} |
+------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Loop of Henle    | - Secondary active transport (major)                                                                                                                      |
|                  | - Passive paracellular diffusion (minor)                                                                                                                  |
| (\~20%)          |                                                                                                                                                           |
|                  | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/12/prize-image002.jpg){fig-alt="Thick ascending limb potassium transport with Na–K–2Cl cotransporter and ROMK"}           |
+------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Collecting ducts | (alpha intercalated cell)                                                                                                                                 |
|                  |                                                                                                                                                           |
| (\~10%)          | - Active transport                                                                                                                                        |
|                  |                                                                                                                                                           |
|                  | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/12/prize-image003.jpg){fig-alt="Alpha intercalated cell hydrogen and potassium transport"}                                |
+------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Secretion:

+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Location              | - Principal cell of the connecting tubule and collecting duct                                                                                 |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Mechanism             | - Secondary active transport                                                                                                                  |
|                       |                                                                                                                                               |
|                       | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/12/prize-image004.jpg){fig-alt="Principal cell sodium and potassium transport through ENaC, ROMK and Maxi-K"} |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Effect of aldosterone | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/12/prize-image005.jpg){fig-alt="Renin–angiotensin pathway through angiotensin subtypes and aldosterone"}      |
|                       |                                                                                                                                               |
|                       | - Stimuli for release:                                                                                                                        |
|                       |   - CRH → ACTH (necessary for synthesis; minor stimulus for release)                                                                          |
|                       |   - Angiotensin 2 (major)                                                                                                                     |
|                       |   - Hyperkalaemia (minor)                                                                                                                     |
|                       | - Effect on principal cell                                                                                                                    |
|                       |   - ↑Na^+^K^+^ATPase synthesis and activity                                                                                                   |
|                       |   - ↑ENaC and ROMK activity                                                                                                                   |
|                       |   - i.e. ↑Na^+^ reabsorption at expense of ↑K^+^ secretion                                                                                    |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Other physiology      | Factors increasing K^+^ secretion:                                                                                                            |
|                       |                                                                                                                                               |
|                       | - ↑ECF \[K^+^\] (↑Na^+^K^+^ATPase activity independent of aldosterone)                                                                        |
|                       | - ↑Urine or Na+ flow rate (e.g. glycosuria)                                                                                                   |
|                       | - ↑Non-Cl^-^ anions                                                                                                                           |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Drugs                 | - Loop diuretics: inhibit Na^+^K^+^2Cl^-^ symporter, hence ↑tubular flow, ↑K^+^ secretion                                                     |
|                       | - Thiazide: inhibit Na^+^Cl^-^ reabsorption in distal convoluted tubule → ↑tubular flow, ↑K^+^ secretion                                      |
|                       | - MR antagonist: ↓Na^+^K^+^ATPase synthesis and activity, ↓ROMK activity → ↓K^+^ secretion                                                    |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Pathology             | - Renal failure: ↓GFR → ↓tubular flow → ↓K^+^ secretion → risk hyperkalaemia                                                                  |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
